newsitem.title: FRANCE: French, German ministers see progress on EMU pact.
newsitem.headline: French, German ministers see progress on EMU pact.

text.p: The finance ministers of France and Germany said on Friday they were making progress on a European "stability pact" limiting budget deficits under monetary union.
"We're advancing," French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said following talks with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel during a Franco-German summit here.
"We have made some progress, but we haven't finished," Waigel told reporters.

France's new Socialist-led government said on Monday it was not ready to approve the stability pact until it had reassurances that Europe would intensify political cooperation to focus on growth and jobs.
European ministers and officials have been racing to put together a compromise solution this week ahead of an EU summit in Amsterdam on Monday and Tuesday.
